To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of ion-channel modulators in the study of Na+-K+ fluxes in cyanobacteria is a robust and effective approach.
the use of ion-channel modulating agents is an effective tool to study Na+- K+ ion fluxes in cyanobacteria.
the ion-channel modulating agents lidocamine and veratridin increase cellular Na+ levels in the cyanobacterium Phormidium uncinatum, whereas amiloride and saxitoxine decreases Na+ and K+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new tool for studying Na+- K+ transport in cyanobacteria.

the development of experimental methods to investigate the role of ion-channel modulating agents in cyanobacterial Na+ and K+-fluxes, and to investigate the role and function of Na+ and/or K+ channels in the cyanobacteria.
the study of the Na+ - K+-ATPase, the Na+-channel, the Na+-H+ antiport and the Na+/K+/H+ exchanger in the cyanobacterium Pseudanabaena galeata.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ion channel modulators can be used as a valuable tool in studying cyanobacterial Na+ and K+, and that this approach may be used for further investigations of cyanobacterial ion fluxes.
the use of ion-channel modulating agents is useful in studies of cyanobacterial ion fluxes.
the ionophores used here are useful tools in the study of the Na+- K+ pump and other Na+ channels of cyanobacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ion channel-modulating agents used in the current study are suitable to investigate Na+ - K+- fluxes in cyanobacterial cells.
ion-channel modulation agents can be used to investigate cyanobacterial Na+ and K+-fluxes, and that the Na+-K+-pump in the plasma membrane plays a central role in cyanobacterial ion regulation.
the ion-channel modulators lidocaine and veratridin, in combination with the channel blockers amiloride and saxitoxine, are suitable for use to investigate Na+ - K + fluxes in cyanobacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the experimental design presented here can be used to assess the role of Na+- and K+-channel activity in cyanobacterial Na+ and K+-fluxes, and to study the effects of channel modulators on these fluxes in cyanobacterial cells.
the use of ion-channel modulating compounds in the study of Na+- K+ ion homeostasis in cyanobacteria is feasible and can be used to further elucidate Na+ and K+-transport pathways in this phylum.
ion channel modulators can be successfully used as experimental tools to study ion fluxes in filamentous cyanobacterial cultures.
